gate_reasoning: Stage 5 scores 0 High and 1 Medium out of 62 claims scored (98.4% Low confidence), making this the weakest-evidenced stage in the run by any measure. The dominant problem is structural: the entire quantitative foundation of the stage rests on four source clusters — (a) a single CodeBlue trade press survey (n=855) providing all specialist experience data, cited 10+ times across all three pain points without any independent cross-validation; (b) PMCare operational figures sourced exclusively from a CodeBlue CEO interview, which then drive all downstream cost models for PP5.1 and PP5.3; (c) BPJS pending claims data from secondary Indonesian news sources (Tempo, Detik, Kompas) rather than BPJS Kesehatan's own published statistics; and (d) an AI vendor's own blog post (InterPixels AI) as the sole source for the 60–75% auto-adjudication rate that anchors the medical review queue sizing. Six auto-low-vendor overrides apply, two chain-of-citations overrides apply (McKinsey cited through a personal blog), and five claims carry explicit [ASSUMED] tags where no source exists. The only adequately sourced claim in the entire stage is the technical feasibility note for graph neural network fraud detection (PMC 2024 + ACM SIGKDD 2025). Deep research should prioritise: (1) fetching BPJS Kesehatan official monthly performance data to replace the Tempo/Detik citations; (2) finding BNM or LIAM industry statistics to cross-validate PMCare volume figures; and (3) sourcing an independent benchmark for APAC TPA auto-adjudication rates to replace the InterPixels AI vendor citation. Without these three fixes, the cost models and frequency claims in PP5.1, PP5.2, and PP5.3 all rest on unverified single trade sources.
